01 / Song setup

Choose Gospel favorites, Christmas, or Classical in Category for familiar written melodies. Selecting a song loads its recorded-kit arrangement and starts playback.

Two notes struck together. In-key major/minor 3rds and 6ths, or perfect 4ths, on separate guitar strings. Paired notes use a straight attack; single notes retain slides and bends. Rests and rhythms stay intact.

Slides stay on one string and arrive in time. Half bend = 1 semitone; full bend = 2. MIDI includes pitch-bend curves; use an instrument that responds to pitch bend.

Gradual builds, phrase peaks and gentle endings across successive notes. Automatic considers tempo, genre and mood. Your melody volume remains the overall level; pitches and timing stay unchanged. Exported MIDI includes these note velocities.

Choose one melody sound from either menu. Live instruments use recorded kits. Automatic kit chooses a live instrument for the song.

Automatic kit is the default: the app chooses recorded acoustic or electric guitar, flute, solo violin, string ensemble, Wurlitzer or a recorded piano tone to suit the song’s style, mood and tempo. The selected sound appears in the menu. You can choose any recorded instrument yourself; your choice stays in effect until you change it. Natural, warm, bright and soft piano choices use the same recorded grand-piano kit with different tone and touch settings. Every melody instrument is a recording: acoustic guitar, electric guitar, flute, violin, string ensemble, Wurlitzer and grand piano each use their own kit. Choose Melody only to hear each sound clearly. Slides and bends follow the written melody.

Recorded flute · about the sound

Ten recorded notes, C4–C7, with blended sustain loops for held melody and solo notes. Other pitches use the nearest recording. A single recorded playing strength; velocity controls loudness and brightness. Natural recorded breath remains. Compact mono 32 kHz adaptation, trimmed with crossfaded loops and measured tuning compensation; embedded for offline playback.

Flute samples: Versilian Studios (VSCO 2), edited by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky in tonejs-instruments, CC BY 3.0. Original sample credits. MIDI uses General MIDI Flute; MIDI exports contain notes and bends, not the recordings.

Recorded violin · about the sound

Fourteen recorded bowed notes, A3–C7, with blended sustain loops for long melody and solo notes. Other pitches use the nearest recording. One recorded playing strength; velocity controls loudness and brightness. Natural bow texture and recorded vibrato remain. Compact mono 32 kHz adaptation, trimmed to about 1.5 seconds or less per note, with crossfaded loops and measured tuning compensation. Embedded for offline playback.

Violin samples: Versilian Studios (VSCO 2), edited by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky in tonejs-instruments, CC BY 3.0. Original sample credits. MIDI uses General MIDI Violin; exported MIDI contains notes and bends, not these recordings.

Recorded electric guitar · about the sound

Seventeen recorded picked notes, C♯2–C6, with blended sustain loops for held melody and solo notes. Other pitches use the nearest recording. One recorded playing strength; velocity controls loudness and brightness. The picked attack is retained and held notes decay naturally. Compact mono 32 kHz adaptation with trimmed attacks, level-stabilized sustain loops and measured tuning compensation. Embedded for offline playback. Solo amp drive and effects still apply.

Electric guitar samples: Karoryfer Samples, edited by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky in tonejs-instruments, CC BY 3.0. Original sample credits. MIDI uses General MIDI Clean Electric Guitar; exported MIDI contains notes and bends, not these recordings.

Recorded Wurlitzer EP200 · about the sound

42 recorded electric-piano samples with four playing-strength zones. Quiet notes use softer recordings; louder notes blend toward stronger reed tones. Some upper notes share recordings between zones. The original A1–C7 key mapping, relative sample levels and tuning corrections are retained. Compact mono 32 kHz adaptation with trimmed attacks and level-stabilized, crossfaded sustain loops. Available for melody, solo and both band piano hands; embedded for offline playback.

Wurlitzer EP200 by Greg Sullivan, SFZ conversion and mapping by kinwie / sfzinstruments, CC BY 3.0. Adapted for compact browser playback and velocity-layer blending. MIDI uses General MIDI Electric Piano 2; exported MIDI contains notes and bends, not these recordings.

Recorded string ensemble · about the sound

18 recorded section notes: five cello, five viola and eight violin recordings. These are ensembles, distinct from the solo violin kit. Registers blend between sections; other pitches use the nearest recording. One recorded playing strength per note; velocity controls loudness and brightness. The same bank supplies band Strings, String pad, Bowed pad, melody and solo. Choose Recorded string ensemble or Recorded string pad for melody and solo. The pad variation has a softer attack, darker tone and longer release. Compact mono 32 kHz adaptation with tuning compensation and blended sustain loops; embedded for offline playback.

VSCO 2 Community Edition, recorded by Sam Gossner and Simon Dalzell; sample cutting by Elan Hickler / Soundemote. Source recordings, CC0. Adapted for compact browser playback. MIDI uses General MIDI String Ensemble; exported MIDI contains notes and bends, not these recordings.

Melody only · extra gain up to 150% (+24 dB). Slide fully left to mute the melody and keep the backing instruments.

Repeating verse and chorus themes, distinct other sections, matched to the key, chords and difficulty. Plays on Piano right hand and appears on the music sheet. Solo is disabled while checked.

Allow in-key diminished chords in generation and chord choices. Existing chords stay in place when unchecked.

Adds a reprise of the chorus (or verse) before the outro, up to 64 bars.

How far sustained notes ring past their slot. Applies to notes marked Sustained (by Auto or by hand).

Automatic: lighter openings and verses, fuller choruses, contrasting bridges, and phrase endings. Explicit bar edits are kept.

Auto uses tempo, section, pattern density and articulation. Slow brushes suit soft, spacious bars; quick strokes suit accents and busy rhythms. The beat stays fixed. Click a bar’s strum pattern to override its attack.

Every strum is played on recorded guitar notes, one per string, with lighter upstrokes and natural string damping. Acoustic: Iowa guitar recordings, edited by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky, CC BY 3.0, sampled every two semitones and stored as lossless FLAC (44.1 kHz). Electric: the recorded electric-guitar kit; amp drive applies.

Recorded single notes for picking. Strums keep their existing sound. Iowa guitar recordings, edited by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky, CC BY 3.0. Adapted to eight anchor notes, mono 32 kHz, up to four-second tails with fades. One recorded playing strength; velocity adjusts volume and brightness. Slides and bends use pitch-shifted playback.

Automatic follows the genre, meter and song form: a steady verse groove, a fuller chorus, a lighter bridge and restrained phrase-end fills. Chord count never changes the groove.

Both piano hands use recordings: the grand piano kit or the Wurlitzer EP200. Melody has its own instrument selection.
Samples: Salamander Grand Piano V3 — Alexander Holm, CC BY 3.0. Compact adaptation: two velocity layers, selected keys, mono 32 kHz PCM, tails shortened to six seconds with fades. Recordings are embedded for offline use; MIDI does not embed samples.

Applies to String pad and Bowed pad. Other pad sounds keep their own voice.

The high-quality sounds need the Sounds folder (Chrome or Edge on a computer); otherwise the built-in strings play. Also used by the Strings melody instrument.

Recorded Hohner Special 20 harmonica: Versilian Community Sample Library, CC0 1.0. Lossless FLAC (44.1 kHz) with seamless sustain loops.

Builds with the song: little or nothing in the intro, fuller in choruses, a fill at phrase ends. High-quality recordings (Sounds folder): Virtuosity Drums percussion (Versilian Studios) and Swirly Drums djembe/darbouka (Karoryfer Samples), CC0 1.0. Without them, drum-kit sounds stand in.

Electric: Growlybass — Karoryfer Samples, CC0 1.0. Upright: VSCO 2 Community Edition contrabass pizzicato, CC0 1.0. Lossless FLAC, mono 32 kHz.

Single-chord bars · Custom strum

Choose D (down), U (up), or – (rest) for each eighth-note position. This row is one complete bar. Changes apply immediately. For double-chord bars, the pattern continues across the chord change.

The first and last bars keep their held chords unless you set a bar strum on the music sheet. Custom patterns are remembered in this browser for each time signature.

Double-chord bars · Custom strum

Choose D (down), U (up), or – (rest) for each eighth-note position. This row is one complete bar. Changes apply immediately. For double-chord bars, the pattern continues across the chord change.

The first and last bars keep their held chords unless you set a bar strum on the music sheet. Custom patterns are remembered in this browser for each time signature.

Metronome accents beat 1; choose Beat one only to hear just the downbeat of every bar. Pick a sound that cuts through your mix, and tick Boost if it still gets buried. Compound meters click on dotted-quarter beats; 7/8 clicks eighth notes in 2 + 2 + 3 groups.

Random Musical Song chooses a coordinated style, key, mode, tempo, length, chords and accompanying instruments using familiar songwriting conventions.

Mixer faders cover only the audible range: 1 is -15 dB (soft), 56 is 0 dB, 100 is +12 dB; 0 mutes. They respond instantly while the song plays. A master limiter keeps loud settings from clipping.

Guitar strums follow the song sections. D = down, U = up, – = rest.

Guitar picking layers over the guitar strumming and drums. Patterns are built from the chord fingering with a clear bass string, and follow chord changes inside each bar.

Pad: sustained chords above middle C with no bass note, so it fills space without adding rhythm. Chorus-only is the safest way to lift a hook.

Strings: a melodic section that plays only above the piano’s right hand, in long notes, so it never muddies the piano.

Bass follows the active chord, including both chords in a split bar, alongside the guitars and drums.

Drum sound · sampled acoustic kit

Kick, snare, three toms, sidestick, closed/open hi-hats, ride and crash use actual acoustic recordings: three playing strengths and two alternating strikes each. Cymbals ring naturally; closing the hi-hat cuts off its open sound. Fills also use a hi-hat foot chick, ride bell, rimshot, flam and snare buzz, and choruses can add a recorded tambourine. Hand claps and sleigh bells are recordings too (VCSL, CC0).

Recordings: Big Rusty Drums — Karoryfer Samples, CC0 1.0; hi-hat foot, ride bell, rimshot, flam, buzz and tambourine: Virtuosity Drums — Versilian Studios, CC0 1.0; hand claps and sleigh bells: Versilian Community Sample Library, CC0 1.0. Selected recordings converted to mono, stored as lossless FLAC (32 kHz; hi-hat foot, ride bell and claps 48 kHz, tambourine and sleigh bells 44.1 kHz) with a short end fade for this offline edition. MIDI exports use General MIDI percussion; their sound depends on your MIDI player.

Drum grooves are selected separately for one-chord and two-chord bars. Off silences the drums for that bar type.

Piano: the left hand carries bass and chord rhythm; the right hand plays a melody or arpeggio line above middle C drawn from the current key and mode. Combine any left hand with any right hand, or set either to Off.

Pop: familiar recurring I–V–vi–IV and vi–IV–I–V families, adapted to your key and mode.

03 / Your chord progression

Variation 1

Tap Select bars, then tap the first and last bars of your section.

Practice a strum

Every distinct pattern used in this song, including your bar edits and held opening/ending strums. Bar numbers show every place each pattern is used. Edits refresh this list automatically. Practice a pattern on its own, looping in the song's time signature. Bold arrows are the accents: the downbeat strongest, then beat-group starts and any stroke that pushes in after a gap. A ━ line after a stroke means it rings through the gap (a hold). Press one to start, press it again (or Stop) to end.

Difficulty controls chord choices: Simple uses only I, vi, IV and V (or their modal equivalents), including split bars; higher levels add more harmonic variety. Fingerings favor practical low-position shapes. In Song mode, every progression begins and ends with the tonic triad of your selected mode (A Ionian: A; A Dorian: Am; Locrian uses a non-diminished substitute). Interior bars are free to use any musically suitable chord, including the tonic when it sounds right. No other bar is required to be I/i. Every click of Generate creates a new complete song, varying interior chords while preserving the opening and closing tonic. Chords are chosen to create purposeful harmonic motion: ii or IV can prepare V7, which resolves to I; occasional deceptive cadences delay arrival. The generator builds recurring four-bar harmonic motifs. Eight-bar sections repeat their motif with a varied ending (A/A′); returning verses and choruses reuse their own original patterns, including chord quality and inner-bar changes except where the song must end on I/i. Longer songs contain recurring verses and choruses. The first and last bars use the home chord; only those bars are required to. Blues mode creates a complete, repeating 12-bar I–IV–V blues and preserves the tonic in the final bar. Some interior bars can hold two chords, placed on strong beats according to the time signature. Occasionally, the first chord of a split bar approaches the second from a root a perfect fifth above it, such as Dm to G in C major or G7 to C. This is selective, not used on every split bar. The first and last bars stay single sustained tonic chords. During playback the diagram automatically follows each chord. Tap a chord when stopped to examine it.

MIDI downloads

Download full song ZIP includes all nine individual instrument MIDI files plus the combined multitrack MIDI. Or check specific parts and use Download selected MIDI ZIP. You can also download an instrument directly using its own button. Piano includes both hands in one MIDI file. Input settings & help
SIGNAL ON EACH CHANNEL

Adjust gain on the Apollo first. Use this only for extra level adjustment.

If your recorded guitar sounds late, move toward +. If it sounds early, move toward −. This changes selected-take playback, not the downloaded WAV. Browser timing is an estimate; input delay is not automatically calibrated.

Browser native is the default that recorded cleanly with your Apollo. It exports WAV after capture; some browsers compress the source audio. PCM is an alternative uncompressed recorder. Tuner and chord analysis pause during recording to reduce processing.

If the input is missing, check the Apollo connection, allow microphone permission, and refresh devices. Only channels exposed by the browser appear here. Listen through Apollo Console; this app does not send live input to your speakers or upload your audio.

09 / Guitar solo

Scale-based lead · tab on paper

The app picks the scale that fits this song, then writes a solo over the bars you choose. Choose Sung line phrasing and the solo is shaped the way a singer would phrase a lyric: it breathes, lands on the strong syllables, and holds the last note of each line. The line follows every chord change, lands chord tones on the strong beats, breathes in phrases, climbs to a peak and comes home. It plays in the arrangement as the Solo guitar part in your band, and it is tabbed out below on sheet paper.

Gold = home note (the key's root) · small red dot = the mode's home note when the scale is a mode · teal = scale notes · ringed notes are the ones this solo uses · the shaded frets are the position the solo sits in · lit notes are sounding while the song plays.

For songs of 16 bars or more. The melody rests for these bars while the band keeps playing, so you can play your solo live.

The same fader as the Solo guitar card in your band.

Choose where the solo goes, then press Write the solo. To put a second solo elsewhere, pick another start bar (and any different scale, density, level or phrasing) and press Write the solo again: solos in different places are kept together.
